en: Majjhima Nikāya 123,
The Discourse on the Wonderful and Marvellous.
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then, after the meal, on returning from their alms round, a number of bhikkhus gathered and assembled in the assembly hall, where this discussion arose:
“It is wonderful, friends, it is marvelous, friends, how great is the psychic power and majesty of the Tathāgata!”
For it is indeed remarkable that the Tathāgata, regarding those Buddhas of the past who have attained final Nibbāna, for whom the proliferations are cut off,

the pathways are severed, the cycle is ended, and who have transcended all suffering, should know: "Those Blessed Ones were of such a birth," and "Those Blessed Ones were of such a name," and "Those Blessed Ones were of such a clan," and "Those Blessed Ones were of such virtue," and "Those Blessed Ones were of such a Dhamma."
‘Those Blessed Ones were such,’ and also, ‘Those Blessed Ones had such wisdom,’ and also,
‘Those Blessed Ones dwelt in such a way,’ and also, ‘Those Blessed Ones were thus liberated.
When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to those bhikkhus:
“Friends, the Tathāgatas are indeed wonderful and endowed with wonderful qualities;
friends, the Tathāgatas are indeed marvelous and endowed with marvelous qualities.
And so this conversation among those bhikkhus remained unfinished.
Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and went to the assembly hall. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Once seated, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
"Bhikkhus, for what discussion are you gathered here now, and what was the conversation that was left unfinished?"
“Here, Bhante, after we had returned from our alms round following the meal, we were sitting gathered together in the assembly hall when this discussion arose among us:

‘It is wonderful, friends! It is marvelous, friends! How great is the Tathāgata’s psychic power and majesty, in that the Tathāgata [knows] the Buddhas of the past who have attained final Nibbāna, whose proliferations are cut off, whose cycles are ended, and whose rounds are exhausted.’”
‘Having transcended all suffering, he will know:

“Those Blessed Ones were of such a birth; they had such names… such clans… such conduct… such qualities… such wisdom… such abodes… and those Blessed Ones were of such liberation,” so it will be. When this was said,
"Venerable sir, the Venerable Ānanda said this to us:
'Friends, the Tathāgatas are indeed wonderful and endowed with wonderful qualities;
friends, the Tathāgatas are indeed marvelous and endowed with marvelous qualities.'"
“Venerable sir, this conversation of ours was left unfinished when the Blessed One arrived.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Therefore, Ānanda, let more wonderful and marvelous qualities of the Tathāgata occur to you.”
“Venerable sir, I have heard this directly from the Blessed One, I have received it directly from the Blessed One:
‘Mindful and clearly comprehending, Ānanda, the Bodhisatta was reborn in the Tusita host.
Venerable sir, that the Bodhisatta was reborn in the Tusita host mindful and clearly comprehending—this too, venerable sir, I remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Blessed One.”
“Face to face with the Blessed One, venerable sir, have I heard and received this:
‘Mindful and clearly comprehending, Ānanda, the Bodhisatta remained in the Tusita realm.
Venerable sir, that the Bodhisatta remained in the Tusita realm mindful and clearly comprehending—this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.”
"Venerable sir, I have heard this directly from the Blessed One; I have received it directly from the Blessed One:
'Ānanda, for as long as his lifespan lasted, the Bodhisatta remained in the Tusita realm.
Venerable sir, that the Bodhisatta remained in the Tusita realm for as long as his lifespan lasted—this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One."
"Face to face with the Blessed One, venerable sir, have I heard this; face to face have I received it:
'Mindful and clearly comprehending, Ānanda, the Bodhisatta passed away from the Tusita realm and descended into his mother’s womb.

That the Bodhisatta, mindful and clearly comprehending, passed away from the Tusita realm and descended into his mother’s womb—this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One."
"Face to face with the Blessed One, venerable sir, have I heard this; face to face have I received it:

'Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta, having passed away from the Tusita realm, descends into his mother’s womb, then in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans, a measureless, sublime radiance appears, surpassing even the splendor of the gods.'"
Even in those intermediate spaces between worlds— void, unsheltered, and shrouded in blinding darkness where even these suns and moons,
so powerful and majestic, do not reach with their radiance— even there a measureless and sublime light appears in the world,
surpassing the splendor of the devas.
"Those beings who have been reborn there also recognize one another by that light, saying: 'Indeed, friends, there are other beings here who have been reborn.
And this ten-thousandfold world-system trembles, shakes, and quakes; and an immeasurable, sublime radiance appears in the world, surpassing even the splendor of the devas.
"Venerable sir, as for this... I too, venerable sir, remember this wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One."
“Bhante, I have heard this directly from the Blessed One; I have received it directly from his presence:
‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, four sons of the gods approach to provide protection in the four directions, thinking:
“Let no human or non-human... [harm] that Bodhisatta or the Bodhisatta’s mother.”’”
‘or anyone who would harm you.
That too, Bhante, … [as before] … this, Bhante, I remember as another wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, Bhante; I received it directly from the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, the Bodhisatta’s mother is naturally virtuous;
she abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech,
and abstains from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which cause heedlessness.’
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this from the Blessed One’s own lips, venerable sir; I received it from his own lips:
‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, no sensual desire arises in the mind of the Bodhisatta’s mother toward men.’”
“...and there arises [a thought] connected with the strands of sensual pleasure; yet the Bodhisatta’s mother remains inviolable by any man with a lustful mind.
This too, Bhante, ...pe... this too, Bhante, I remember as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, Bhante, and received it directly from him:

‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, the Bodhisatta’s mother becomes a recipient of the five strands of sensual pleasure. Endowed and possessed of these five strands of sensual pleasure, she enjoys herself.
That too, Bhante, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One...
I heard this from the Blessed One’s own lips, Bhante; I received it directly from the Blessed One’s own lips:
“Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, no affliction whatsoever arises for the Bodhisatta’s mother;
the Bodhisatta’s mother is happy and her body is free from fatigue; and the Bodhisatta’s mother sees the Bodhisatta within her womb, complete in all limbs and faculties.”
“Ānanda, it is just as if there were a beautiful beryl gem, of pure birth, with eight facets, well-polished. A thread were strung through it, blue, or yellow, or red, or white, or pale yellow.
A man with good sight, having taken it in his hand, would examine it: ‘This indeed is a beautiful beryl gem, of pure birth, with eight facets, well-polished;
and here is this thread strung through it, blue, or yellow, or red…’”
or white, or yellowish-white.
Even so, Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta has descended into his mother’s womb, no affliction whatsoever arises in the Bodhisatta’s mother;
the Bodhisatta’s mother is happy and her body is free from fatigue; and as for the Bodhisatta...
“The mother of a Bodhisatta sees [the child] within her womb, complete with all limbs and faculties, with no sense organ lacking.
This too, Bhante, ... [as before] ... this, Bhante, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, Bhante; I received it directly from the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, seven days after the Bodhisatta is born, the Bodhisatta’s mother passes away and reappears in the Tusita heaven.
As for this, Bhante … [as before] … I also, Bhante, remember this wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, Bhante; I received it directly from the Blessed One:
“However, Ānanda, unlike other women who give birth after carrying the fetus in their womb for nine or ten months,
the Bodhisatta’s mother does not give birth in that way. For exactly ten months,
the Bodhisatta’s mother carries the Bodhisatta in her womb and then gives birth.”
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...I remember this as another wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
Venerable sir, I heard this in the presence of the Blessed One and received it from his own lips:
‘Ānanda, whereas other women give birth while sitting or lying down, the mother of a Bodhisatta does not give birth in such a way; rather, the mother of a Bodhisatta gives birth while standing.’”
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, I received it directly from the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, the deities receive him first, and afterwards human beings.’”
"Furthermore, Bhante... [as before] ...this too, Bhante, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this from the Blessed One’s own mouth, Bhante; I received it directly from the Blessed One’s own mouth:
'Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, even before he has reached the ground...'"
When he was born, four sons of gods received him and placed him before his mother, saying: “Be joyful, O Queen!
A son of great power has been born to you.
Venerable sir, as for this... [as before] ...this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
"Face to face with the Blessed One, venerable sir, have I heard this; face to face have I received it:
'Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, he emerges quite clean, unsmeared by water, unsmeared by mucus, unsmeared by blood, unsmeared by any impurity—pure and clean.
Just as, Ānanda, a precious gem placed upon a Kāsī cloth does not smear the Kāsī cloth, nor does the Kāsī cloth smear the precious gem.'"
And why is that? Because both are pure.

In the same way, Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, he emerges quite clean, unsullied by water, unsullied by mucus, unsullied by blood, and unsullied by any impurity; he is pure and clean.”
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...this, venerable sir, I remember as another wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
I heard this directly from the Blessed One, venerable sir, and received it directly from him:

‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, two streams of water appear from the sky—one cool and one warm—with which they perform the water-rites for the Bodhisatta and for his mother.’”
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...I remember this as another wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
Venerable sir, I have heard this in the presence of the Blessed One; it was received by me directly from his presence:
‘Ānanda, as soon as the Bodhisatta was born, he stood with both feet firmly planted on the ground, facing north.’”
He walks with the stride of a lion, with a white parasol held over him, he surveys all directions, and he utters this lion’s roar:
“I am the foremost in the world; I am the eldest in the world; I am the best in the world.
This is my final birth; now there is no more renewed existence.”
“Venerable sir, that too... [as before] ...this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
Venerable sir, I heard this in the presence of the Blessed One; I received it in his presence:
‘Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta emerges from his mother’s womb, then in the world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās...’”
A boundless, sublime radiance appears in the world for the generation with its recluses and brahmins,
its devas and humans, surpassing even the splendor of the devas.
Even those intermediate spaces between the worlds— those regions of gloom, impenetrable darkness, and blinding blackness where even these suns and moons [do not reach]...
Though they possess such great psychic power and such great majesty, they do not outshine [the Buddha] with their radiance.
Even there, a measureless and sublime effulgence appears in the world, surpassing even the divine power of the gods.
And those beings who have been reborn there also recognize one another by that light, saying: "It seems, friends, that there are other beings who have been reborn here as well."
"And this ten-thousandfold world system trembles, shakes, and quakes; and an immeasurable, sublime radiance appears in the world, surpassing even the splendor of the devas.
"Venerable sir, as for this... [and so on]... Venerable sir, I also remember this wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
"Therefore, Ānanda, you should also remember this wonderful and marvelous quality of the Tathāgata."
"In this case, Ānanda, feelings are known by the Tathāgata as they arise, known as they persist, and known as they pass away;
perceptions are known as they arise … [as above] … thoughts are known as they arise, known as they persist, and known as they pass away."
“Ānanda, you should also remember this as a marvelous and wonderful quality of the Tathāgata.
“Venerable sir, when feelings are known by the Blessed One as they arise, known as they persist, and known as they pass away;
when perceptions are known… [and so on].”
“Thoughts arise known, they persist known, and they pass away known.
This, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
Thus spoke the Venerable Ānanda.
The Teacher gave his approval,
and those bhikkhus, being satisfied, rejoiced in the words of the Venerable Ānanda.
The Third Discourse on the Wonderful and Marvellous is finished.
